display.purpose: The PokéCipher wordmark only. Press Start 2P has no comfortable reading size.

headline.purpose: Section headings. Still Press Start 2P, still only a few words at a time.

body.purpose: Hero copy, terminal transcript, decoded results. VT323 carries everything that is read.

label.purpose: Field labels, character counters, helper text. Uppercase with open tracking.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: The terminal block cursor. Hard on/off with steps(); never a fade.

motion.name: color-only
motion.purpose: The only permitted state transition. Colour shifts, never lift, scale or blur.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single yellow-filled element on the page. Reserved for the main action.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; white-space: nowrap; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; font-family: var(--font-terminal), VT323, ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 14px; border-width: 1px; border-style: solid; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #8bac0f; } .ds-btn-primary { background: #ffd100; color: #0f380f; border-color: #ffd100; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #e6bc00; border-color: #e6bc00; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Equal-weight alternate action. Moss fill, washed text.

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Tertiary action. Border only, no fill until hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: #d7f5c4; border-color: #2c5c2c; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #265626; } .ds-btn-outline:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Terminal Panel
components.description: The signature component. Chrome bar over a transcript body; interior goes darker than the page so it reads as a recessed screen. Shown here with the required cartridge-yellow border, which is not yet in the implementation.
components.html:
bash

$ encode "Try below"

Persian Farfetch'd Shellder Bulbasaur Machoke

type a message below, or "help"

$
components.css: .ds-terminal { border: 1px solid #ffd100; background: #071a07; font-family: var(--font-terminal), VT323, ui-monospace, monospace; } .ds-terminal-chrome { background: #265626; color: #d7f5c4; border-bottom: 1px solid #2c5c2c; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 14px; } .ds-terminal-body { padding: 16px; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.375; } .ds-terminal-body p { margin: 0 0 2px; } .ds-prompt { color: #ffd100; } .ds-line-cmd { color: #d7f5c4; } .ds-line-out { color: #8bac0f; } .ds-line-info { color: #9bbc8a; } .ds-cursor { display: inline-block; width: 12px; height: 20px; background: #ffd100; vertical-align: text-bottom; animation: ds-blink 1.1s steps(1, end) infinite; } @keyframes ds-blink { 0%, 49% { opacity: 1; } 50%, 100% { opacity: 0; } }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Square, bordered, recessed. Focus is an olive ring; the border colour does not change.
components.html: <textarea class="ds-input" rows="3" placeholder="Type a message, or paste Pokemon names to decode."></textarea>
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #1d4d24; color: #d7f5c4; border: 1px solid #2c5c2c; border-radius: 0; padding: 12px; font-family: var(--font-terminal), VT323, ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 16px; resize: vertical; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #9bbc8a; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #8bac0f; }

components.name: Token Chip
components.description: One unit of ciphertext as its name. The fallback when sprites are off or a sprite fails to load — a first-class state, not an error.
components.css: .ds-token { display: inline-block; background: rgba(38, 86, 38, 0.6); color: #d7f5c4; border: 1px solid #2c5c2c; border-radius: 0; padding: 2px 6px; font-family: var(--font-terminal), VT323, ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; }

components.name: Decoder Markers
components.description: The product's most distinctive output. Amber is genuine ambiguity, coral is a state mismatch, ice is an unknown name. Coral currently fails contrast and needs raising.
components.html: Hello W[n,o]rld! and a {x,y} plus <?unknown: Mewtwo>
components.css: .ds-markers { background: #14421a; border: 1px solid #2c5c2c; padding: 12px; margin: 0; color: #d7f5c4; font-family: var(--font-terminal), VT323, ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 16px; line-height: 2; } .ds-marker-ambiguous { color: #e8b93b; font-weight: 600; } .ds-marker-mismatch { color: #e0674f; font-weight: 600; } .ds-marker-unknown { color: #7fb3d5; font-weight: 600; }

narrative.overview:
A researcher's command line for reading Pokédex data. The cipher is not presented as a toy trick but as instrument output: you type at a prompt, the machine answers in a transcript, and when the machine is uncertain it says so in its own notation rather than guessing. The $ prompt, the monospace transcript and the blinking block cursor are the spine of the identity.

The surface is a four-tone Game Boy LCD. Depth is carried entirely by stepped greens — five of them, from near-black #0f380f up to #2c5c2c — with no shadows and no rounded corners anywhere. One warm colour, cartridge yellow, exists in an otherwise wholly green world, which is why it can mean something.

This world is semi-settled and explicitly iterative. The Game Boy greens are good but not sacred: they hold until they fail the squint test or something better earns the place. The type pairing was a ship-fast choice and self-hosted retro faces have not been explored. Treatments here are meant to be tried, looked at, and reversed without ceremony — a reversal is the process working.
keyCharacteristics: Four-tone LCD green, tonal depth, zero shadow, zero radius
One warm accent (#ffd100) in an otherwise green system
Terminal transcript as the primary voice
Uncertainty rendered as notation, never hidden

rules.name: The One Warm Thing Rule
rules.body: Yellow is the only warm colour permitted in the chrome. If a second warm accent appears, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Signal Reservation Rule
rules.body: Amber, coral and ice mean decoder states and nothing else. Never reuse a signal colour for form validation, hover, or emphasis — an empty-input error must not borrow coral from corrupted ciphertext.

rules.name: The Pixel Sparingly Rule
rules.body: Press Start 2P appears at the wordmark and section headings only. It has no lowercase rhythm and no comfortable reading size; using it for more than a few words is a legibility failure, not a stylistic one.

rules.name: The Open Pairing Rule
rules.body: This pairing is provisional. Self-hosted retro faces have not been evaluated, and the pairing may be replaced — but only by another retro/pixel pairing, never by a neutral grotesque.

rules.name: The Grouping Rule
rules.body: Space communicates relationship. Elements that belong together are closer to each other than to anything else, and no gap inside a group may exceed the gap around it.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. Separation comes from tone and border, never from blur.

rules.name: The No-Curve Rule
rules.body: A radius above 0px anywhere is a defect. The Game Boy could not draw one.

dos: Do keep yellow scarce. It marks the prompt, the cursor, the primary action, and the terminal's border. Nothing else.
Do render decoder uncertainty as visible notation. [x,y] and {x,y} are the product's most distinctive output.

Do let colour carry meaning on its own where that is the stronger design. No blanket rule applies in either direction here; decide case by case. A control that needs a tooltip to explain itself has failed visually.
Do use space to group. Related elements sit closer together than unrelated ones.
Do keep every surface bordered and flat.
Do treat treatments as reversible experiments.
donts: Don't add soft, blurred or ambient shadows. (A hard pixel-offset block is a separate, permitted experiment.)
Don't introduce any corner radius above 0px.
Don't add Geist, Inter, Instrument Serif, JetBrains Mono, or any neutral grotesque. Retro faces only.
Don't put the three macOS traffic-light dots on the terminal chrome.
Don't place the kicker above the wordmark; it sits below.
Don't reuse a decoder signal colour for anything that is not a decoder state.
Don't set body copy in Press Start 2P.
Don't ship #e0674f, #b03a2e, or #9bbc8a-on-#265626 at their current contrast; all three fail AA where they are used.
